claims.evidence: The witness sees a rear derailleur but the number of gears on the cassette and chainrings was not counted.
The witness identifies it as a road bike but cannot confirm the frame material from the photo.
Requires a dated receipt or original purchase documentation.
The witness report explicitly lists gear shifting and brake responsiveness as 'not shown'.
The witness sees the bike from a distance; close-ups of the chain, bolts, and drivetrain are missing.
Cannot be verified without identifying the specific model and comparing it to factory specifications.

risks.risk: Structural frame damage (cracks or dents hidden by paint/decals)
risks.proof: A slow, close-up video walk-around of all frame welds and tubes.
risks.if_unproven: as a compromised frame with scrap value only.

risks.risk: Worn or skipping drivetrain (chain and cassette wear)
risks.proof: A video of the bike being ridden or pedaled by hand while shifting through all gears.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a full drivetrain replacement (chain, cassette, and potentially chainrings).

risks.proof: A video of each wheel spinning freely to check for lateral wobble.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring professional wheel truing or rim replacement.

risks.risk: Seized seat post or bottom bracket
risks.proof: A video showing the seat post being adjusted and the cranks spinning smoothly without noise.

proof_requests: Clear, close-up photos of the brand name and model name on the frame.
A photo of the gear shifters and the rear cassette to count the speeds.
A video showing the gears shifting and the brakes stopping the wheels.
Close-up photos of the tire sidewalls to check for dry rot or brand info.
response.reason: The brand and model are completely unknown, making it impossible to establish even a worst-case baseline value for a road bike in the Lagos market.
